findings.claim: The ranking of lateral versus heading start errors computed here predicts which error dominates the endpoint error of real tool or vehicle paths on physical curved parts

hypothesis: On a constant-K background a curvature change at arclength s moves j_lat(L) with weight sn(L-s) cn(s), which decreases along the path when K <= 0 or sqrt(K) L <= pi/2 (before the first focal distance), and j_head(L) with weight sn(L-s) sn(s), which is symmetric about mid-path for every K and vanishes at both ends; exactly, reversing the curvature profile leaves j_head(L) unchanged. The two columns therefore respond differently to where curvature sits along a path and can order paths differently.
input_data: 14 declared paths: plane, sphere, cylinder, saddle, torus, gaussian-bump, hyperbolic-plane, sphere-great-circle, hyperbolic-long, torus-outer-equator, torus-inner-equator, bump-radial, torus-outer-to-inner, torus-inner-to-outer
Witness pair torus-outer-to-inner / torus-inner-to-outer: same torus, same length 3, curvature order reversed but not mirror profiles
Curvature bump of amplitude 0.001, width 0.3 at s in [0.5, 1.5, 2.5] on a flat path of length 3.0
mathematical_model: Endpoint normal displacement = j_lat(L) delta_perp + j_head(L) delta_alpha; delta j(L) = -int G(L, s) j(s) delta K(s) ds with G(L, s) = j_lat(s) j_head(L) - j_head(s) j_lat(L); reversal maps Phi(L) to D Phi(L)^-1 D; model spaces give j_head/j_lat = tan(sqrt(K)L)/sqrt(K), L, tanh(sqrt(-K)L)/sqrt(-K).
numerical_result: Kendall tau 0.264 with 33 discordant pairs; witness lateral 0.8568 vs 1.803, heading 3.907 vs 2.846; finite-difference confirmation error 1.87e-06; bump response lateral early/late 4.94, heading early/late asymmetry 1.74e-11; reversal reciprocity error 1.23e-11.
observation_model: |j(L)| per unit perturbation; confirmed on the witness pair by central differences of perturbed geodesics (eps = 0.001); reversed paths start at the end point with negated velocity.
